content: Stanley Medical College (SMC) is a government-run medical institution located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. While the associated hospital has a history spanning over two centuries, the medical college itself was officially established on July 2, 1938. It is ranked 9th among India's top medical colleges, as per NDTV rankings. The origins of Stanley Medical College and its associated hospitals date back to 1740, when the East India Company established a medical department. The current Stanley Hospital is situated on the site of the Monegar Choultry, which was founded in 1782. In 1809, the Assistant John Native Infirmary was established, incorporating the Monegar Choultry and a leper asylum. In 1830, Raja Sir Ramasamy Mudaliar, a noted philanthropist, endowed a hospital and dispensary within the Native Infirmary. By 1836, Madras University had introduced medical courses such as M.B. & G.M. and L.M. & S. at the infirmary. In 1903, a hospital assistant course was initiated with the support of the East India Company. The first batch of students graduated with Licensed Medical Practitioner (LMP) diplomas in 1911. In 1933, a five-year Diploma in Medicine and Surgery (D.M. & S.) program was launched, and the institution was named after Sir George Fredrick Stanley, the then-Governor of Madras Presidency. By 1941, the college had three medical and surgical units, which expanded to seven by 1964. The college began admitting 100 students annually in 1932, and this number increased to 150 in 1963. In 1964, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the President of India, laid the foundation stone for the college auditorium during its Silver Jubilee celebrations. Stanley Medical College is affiliated with the Government Stanley Hospital, which has 1,580 inpatient beds and an outpatient attendance of approximately 5,000 patients daily. A unique feature of the hospital is its eight-story surgical complex, capable of conducting up to 40 surgeries simultaneously. Additionally, the hospital has a dedicated pediatrics block housing all pediatric specialties under one roof. The institution is renowned for its departments of Surgical Gastroenterology, Urology, and the Institute of Hand Rehabilitation and Plastic Surgery (IRRH & DPS). The IRRH & DPS is considered one of the premier centers for hand rehabilitation and plastic surgery in Southeast Asia. The Department of Surgical Gastroenterology was the first in India to perform a successful liver transplant, under the leadership of Dr. R.P. Shanmugam. It was also the first hospital department in India to receive ISO 9001 certification. The Department of Urology performs up to 50 kidney transplants annually. Admissions to the MBBS program and postgraduate courses (MD, MS, and other diplomas) are highly competitive. Indian citizens are eligible to apply, with 85% of seats reserved for state-level candidates and 15% for national-level candidates. Seats are also reserved for underserved communities, with reduced tuition fees. Admission to the MBBS program, which has approximately 150 seats annually, is based on a combination of entrance exam scores and high school final exam results. The acceptance rate for the MBBS program at Stanley Medical College is less than 1 in 200, making it one of the most selective medical colleges in India. Several postgraduate seats are reserved for physicians serving in government roles. The undergraduate program includes the Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS), a five-and-a-half-year course comprising 4. Postgraduate programs include three-year residency-based MD and MS degrees in various specialties such as General Medicine, Microbiology, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, Dermatology, General Surgery, Anatomy, and Ophthalmology. Two-year postgraduate diploma programs are also offered in fields like Gynecology and Obstetrics, Child Health, Medical Radio Diagnosis, Laryngo-Otology, Anesthesiology, Orthopedics, Ophthalmology, and Dermatology. Higher specialty fellowship programs include DM (Neurology, Cardiology) and MCh (Neurosurgery, Plastic Surgery). The college is associated with several hospitals, including the Government Stanley Hospital, Government Raja Sir Ramasamy Mudaliar (RSRM) Lying-in Hospital, Government Hospital for Thoracic Medicine in Tambaram, and the Government Peripheral Hospital in Tondiarpet. Notable alumni and faculty of Stanley Medical College include Prof. R. Venkataswami, founder of the IRRH & DPS; Dr. V.S. Ramachandran, a renowned brain researcher; Dr. T. Thomas, a cardiothoracic surgeon; Dr. Mohammed Rela, a liver transplant surgeon at King’s College Hospital; Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, founder of Apollo Hospitals; Dr. David Jayakar, Director of Cardiothoracic Surgery in Chicago, USA; and Dr. Dilaawar Mistry, Co-Medical Director of Sports Medicine at the University of Virginia. The college fosters a strong sense of community among its students, with an annual alumni reunion, Old Stanleans Day, held on the last Sunday of January. Each MBBS batch adopts a unique name based on their year of entry, such as Jalaccans 1991 or Aesclepius 1999. Student life at SMC is vibrant, with a variety of extracurricular activities. The college has a music group that has won numerous awards at inter-college cultural festivals. Euphoria, the annual inter-college cultural festival, attracts participants from across the country. The college also has hockey, football, and cricket teams. Students publish a monthly magazine, the Stanley Times, and participate in the Stanley Literary Society, which promotes literature and arts. The Rotaract Club provides free medical services to underserved communities. The college also hosts a National Cadet Corps (NCC) unit affiliated with the Tamil Nadu NCC's medical division. Student facilities include separate hostels for male and female students, with dedicated dining and kitchen facilities for undergraduates, house surgeons, and postgraduates. The campus features sports facilities such as a cricket turf pitch, a basketball court, and table tennis courts. The campus was once known for its lush greenery, but many trees were cut down in 2007 to accommodate expansion, altering the campus's aesthetic and environmental appeal.
